Subject: Onramp cohort — retention credits and alumni extension

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood’s latency profile. We’re running a 12-week onramp cohort for early customers and are trying to structure an incentive that keeps participants active after week 6.

Quick ask: can Redwood allocate a 3-month incremental credit pool that vests in two parts — 60% as immediate onboarding credits and 40% reserved as retention credits that unlock if the company stays active (500 reqs/month) in month 2 and month 3? Our legal team also wants clarity on whether the unused retention portion can roll into alumni credits for startups that graduate into our paid tier.

We’re on a tight timeline — cohort kickoff is 9/7. Can you share a workable terms outline and any standard tooling you use to enforce the unlock conditions?

Appreciate it,
Susan Park
VP, Partnerships — GreenByte Labs

Hi Susan — great to hear the cohort is moving fast. We can support a split pool like you describe; below is a high-level, non-binding proposal so your legal/ops folks have something concrete to review. I’ve attached a short terms doc and a sample MA (Merchant Agreement) spreadsheet that shows the credit math.

Summary proposal (draft):
- Total promotional pool: $30,000 worth of hosted credits.
- Allocation: 60% ($18k) onboarding credits available immediately; 40% ($12k) retention pool gated by activity.
- Unlock rules: retention tranche releases in two equal monthly unlocks of $6k each, contingent on >=500 API requests in each qualifying month. Activity is measured by token-equivalent usage and verified in Redwood Console.
- Alumni rollover: any unused retention credits after month 3 convert to a 12-month alumni discount voucher (30% off list) applied to the account’s first paid invoice, unless GreenByte elects to reassign credits to a different cohort participant (must be specified in the MA).
- Enforcement/automation: Redwood can attach a policy to the customer’s account that evaluates the 500-req threshold and auto-issues the tranche; we can also generate an audit log and send a webhook to your ops address for confirmation.

I’ve CC’d Monica (Customer Success) to confirm operational feasibility and Ben (Sales) to align on the commercial framing. Monica — are the unlock checks straightforward from Console? Ben — want to confirm the proposed pool size and that this fits within the onramp promo guardrails.

If this is acceptable, we’ll produce a version of the terms suitable for signature (DocuSign) and include the conditional automation config.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jordan / Monica — quick thoughts:
- Commercial: $30k for the cohort sounds reasonable but recommend a per-startup cap of $5k to avoid concentration risk (8 startups x $5k = $40k ceiling; we can structure a not-to-exceed clause in the MA). If they intend to fund 12 teams but only 8 active, the per-startup cap prevents accidental over-commitment.
- Promo guardrail: marketing has a stretch bucket but we should flag that alumni rollover into a voucher is limited to 6 months post-graduation unless escalated.
- Legal: we can include two acceptance triggers: (a) console verification (auto) and (b) manual override by Redwood CS with audit trail — useful when usage is atypical.

Monica — can you confirm the webhook + auto-issue path? If yes, I’m comfortable signing off to present this to GreenByte with the per-startup cap and a DocuSign link.

Subject: Final draft: Onramp retention credit structure (proposal & next steps)

Hi Susan — thanks for the quick patience while we checked internally. Below is the final, signable proposal (non-binding until DocuSign completion):

Proposal highlights:
- Pool: $30,000 promotional credits tied to GreenByte’s 12-week onramp cohort.
- Per-startup cap: $5,000 (Redwood will not issue more than $5k to any single participant without written approval).
- Allocation: 60% onboarding ($18k immediate), 40% retention ($12k) released as two $6k tranches.
- Unlock: each $6k tranche releases when the covered startup records >=500 API requests in the qualifying month (measured by token-equivalent calls). The Console rule will evaluate usage at the end of each calendar month; if the threshold is met, we auto-issue the tranche and send a webhook to ops@greenbyte.com.
- Alumni rollover: any unused retention credits after month 3 convert to a 6-month alumni voucher (30% off next paid invoice), unless GreenByte requests reassignment in writing.
- Verification fallback: Redwood CS can manually release a tranche with a recorded justification in the account audit log.

Next steps:
1) Susan/Legal — review and confirm acceptance of the per-startup cap and 6-month alumni voucher window.
2) If accepted, sign via DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/rooms/XYZ-123-Onramp-Terms
3) Monica/CS — I’ll need the webhook endpoint and contact for audit events to wire into the automation.
4) Ben — please confirm final MA spreadsheet numbers; I’ve attached updated MA plan showing per-startup math.

If you want, I can also propose a shorter verification window (e.g., 14-day rolling checks) but that may increase false positives; happy to discuss.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the cohort started next week.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
